tfn.s: Eurostat found that 89.3% of people aged 16 to 29 in the EU had used social networks.
tfn.why: The text says: "Eurostat reported in April 2026 that 89.3% of people aged 16 to 29 in the EU had used social networks during 2025."

tfn.s: A person's habits show what kind of person they are.

tfn.s: The writer would agree that a person's birth year tells you little about their income or health.
tfn.why: Differences within a cohort are "usually larger than the average gap" between cohorts.

tfn.s: The writer treats the Eurostat figures as proof that generational stereotypes are accurate.
tfn.why: The writer calls it a difficulty when "a measured behaviour is promoted into a personality".

tfn.s: The National Academies review recommended replacing generational categories with age bands.
tfn.why: The text gives its conclusion but no recommended alternative.

tfn.s: The article would classify the effect of a new platform used by every age group as a period effect, not a cohort effect.
tfn.why: Period effects "reach everyone at once, as a pandemic or a new platform does".

tfn.s: The article suggests generational labels last mainly because strong evidence supports them.
tfn.why: It says they survive "partly because they are convenient and partly because they sell".

speak.title: Role-play: planning a weekend away
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You want to plan a family weekend away. You prefer to phone people and talk. Ask your grandson to join a call tonight. Listen to his reasons and agree on a way to plan.

b.text: You prefer to send one message to the group chat. Explain why this works for you. Say what you don't like about long phone calls, then look for a fair solution.

phrases: I'd rather talk on the phone, if that's okay.
I didn't mean to upset you.
It's quicker for me to send a message.
Let's try it your way first.
How would you prefer to arrange this?
Could we do both, a message and then a call?
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: what did you agree, and was the compromise fair to both sides?
